A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same RLHF survey. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 presents conceptual taxonomies and summaries of published methods, theoretical guarantees, and empirical findings. It reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical dataset analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Its expanded tables, dataset descriptions, and reported findings synthesize other studies rather than introduce original empirical results.

M1.justification: The general RLHF procedure is retained. v2 expands descriptions of existing approaches, including direct policy optimization, but introduces no new algorithm or model proposed by this work. Corrections to the mathematical exposition do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: New Section 8.4 catalogs feedback datasets, and Section 8.3 expands discussion of offline benchmarks. These resources are surveyed; neither version actually uses datasets for its own training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. Expanded literature-comparison tables classify published approaches without conducting comparative experiments.

E3.justification: Neither version conducts an original evaluation with experimental settings to revise. The evaluation discussion moves from Section 7.4 to Section 8.5 while retaining its policy- and reward-model evaluation examples.

E4.justification: Neither version presents ablations, robustness tests, or experimental case studies conducted for this work. Added taxonomies and discussions of failure conditions are literature synthesis rather than newly performed supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: No run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or statistical tests are introduced. Previously quoted agreement statistics, including 77% ± 2% and 72.6 ± 1.5%, remain unchanged in Section 4.2.2.

E6.justification: v2 adds qualitative findings from cited studies, including Askell et al.'s comparison favoring rankings over binary comparisons in Section 3.2.1 and Bansal et al.'s rating-versus-ranking disagreement in Section 4.2.2. These extend the reported literature evidence; they are not original experiments or measured performance gains by this paper.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the Q- and V-function definitions in Section 2.1 and reverses the erroneous preference-loss exponent in Section 5.2.1. It also revises the loss arguments, specifies an e-stop grounding function, and adds A-PARL's assumptions and O(1/T) bound to Table 6. These are localized mathematical corrections and additions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: a broad survey of RLHF fundamentals, developments, and applications beyond LLMs, continuing the earlier PbRL survey literature. Expanded coverage does not redefine this core claim.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands guidance on choosing and combining feedback, explains weaknesses of volume-removal query selection, and discusses policy-training problems from nonstationary and approximate rewards. Its conclusion adds concrete limitations involving human judgment, spurious correlations, and separation of policy and reward models, beyond v1's more general qualifications.

D1.justification: Section 8.2 adds a link to Clean-Offline-RLHF. New Section 8.4 provides access links for public feedback datasets, including hh-rlhf, SHP, HelpSteer, and Uni-RLHF. This expands practical resource-access information without adding an experimental implementation.

R1.justification: The literature synthesis expands substantially across natural-language feedback, query selection, offline RLHF, policy optimization, and Nash learning. Tables 2 and 3 add discussions of Retzlaff et al., Fernandes et al., and Yuan et al. These substantive additions go beyond the numerous bibliographic metadata updates.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting accompanies regrouping feedback classes, reorganizing query-selection explanations, and moving v1's Direct Methods subsection into the expanded Policy Learning chapter. However, v2 also contains an unfinished editorial note in Section 3.2.2 and broken prose in the conclusion.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different typographic layout. v1's two diagrams are redrawn and combined into v2 Figure 1, with section-specific variants added as Figures 2–5. Table 4 gains explicit feedback groupings, and a new Table 5 summarizes query-selection strategies.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the survey's instructional completeness and mathematical reliability. Section 6 fills a meaningful gap in policy-training coverage, while Sections 2.1 and 5.2.1 correct erroneous value-function definitions and the preference-loss sign. Expanded feedback-selection guidance and concrete limitations strengthen its practical usefulness. Unremoved drafting text and broken sentences reduce polish, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
